sentences.text:
Heard Mr. Rajeev Kumar Singh, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State opposite party 1 and Mr. Mohit Singh, the learned counsel representing first informant opposite party 2, who has put in appearance by filing his vakalatanama in Court today, which is taken on record.
Perused the record.

Applicant Dal Bahadur Singh, who is a charge sheeted accused, has approached this Court by means of present application under Section 482 Cr. P. C. with the following prayer:-
Prashant Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69954888/

sentences.text:
"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to allow the present application and to quash the impugned order dated 23.10.2024 passed by the learned Trial Court/Additional Session, Special Judge (POCSO Act) Sant Kabir Nagar in Special Session Trial No. 311/2022 (State Vs.
Prashant Singh) arising out of Case Crime No. 125/2022 u/s 363, 366, 376, 304 I.P.C.
and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Khalilabad, District Sant Kabir Nagar.

sentences.text:
It is, further prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be graciously be pleased to stay the effect and operation of the impugned order dated 23.10.2024 passed by the learned Trial Court/Additional Session, Special Judge (POCSO Act) Sant Kabir Nagar in Special Session Trial No. 311/2022 (State Vs. Prashant Singh) arising out of Case Crime No. 125/2022 u/s 363, 366, 376, 304 I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Khalilabad, District Sant Kabir Nagar as well as further proceeding of aforesaid case/trial, pending in the Court of AdditionalSession, Special Judge (POCSO Act)
Sant Kabir Nagar, during the pendency of the present case before this Hon'ble Court.

entities.text: Special Session Trial No. 311/2022 (State Vs. Prashant Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And/or pass such other and further orders which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the circumstances of the case."
At the very outset, the learned counsel for applicant submits that by efflux of time, the present application has been rendered infructuous.
He, therefore, submits that present application be accordingly dismissed as having rendered infructuous.
Learned A.G.A. and Mr. Mohit Singh, the learned counsel representing first informant opposite party 2 have no objection to the prayer made by the learned counsel for applicant.
In view of above, this application is, accordingly, dismissed as having rendered infructuous.
Interim order, if any, stands discharged.
